hypothesis: The exact ADR1076 preparation implementation preserves acquired coverage, error precedence and input state over previously unexecuted multi-step session/store, layered-fault and adjacent-view sequences; a successful cached value never crosses an identity or invalidation boundary.
comparison_scope: MAIN104 versus byte-identical ADR1076 candidate; mechanical finite synthetic contract only. This is not a legal-quality holdout and does not replace the separately declared native replay.
novelty_against_1076: ADR1076 used static states and isolated named transitions. These new cases enumerate five-position session/store braids, persistent failure and repair cycles, all application/restoration orders of three simultaneous faults, and bypass-return-adjacent-view cycles. No old case IDs or cases are relabeled. No ADR1076 fixture or runner is imported.

identity_braid.sequence: At each of five route positions, select the declared session/store identity, optionally start a new view, then call twice with equal input values. Revalidation is required on any identity change or new view; the immediate repeat is eligible for reuse.

layered_fault_orders.restoration_orders: all 6 permutations independently of application order
layered_fault_orders.sequence: Success twice; apply each of the three faults in order and call after each; repeat the fully faulted state; restore each component in order and call after each; repeat fully restored state; new-view success twice. Active ACL error takes precedence over source-block error, then span error, irrespective of mutation order.

comparison: Exact typed values and ordered gathered spans at every call, or exact exception class name and message
Predeclared semantic coverage/error oracle for both arms, including concurrent-fault precedence
All session/store input state unchanged by every product call; explicit fixture transitions remain visible
Fresh fixture per arm; no shared runtime module or mutable object across arms
Any session/store identity change or new view performs the baseline number of source reads
Failed validation attempts and bypass states perform the baseline number of source reads
A first call after bypass restoration performs the baseline number of source reads
Eligible immediate successful repeats avoid source reads while performing exactly one immutable-store check
At least one successful reuse witness and a fresh-boundary witness in each category

acl_or_missing_source: delivered reference source outside current scope

failure_policy: Write each complete paired trace and flush lossless compressed raw data. Preserve the first failure with the paired trace and partial census; do not overwrite any existing raw or failure output. Do not revise expected outputs or candidate after observing results; a changed hypothesis requires a follow-up ADR.
limits: Finite sequential synthetic source contracts only; no concurrent source mutation or arbitrary adapter behavior
Stores expose an immutable check_unchanged capability; injected source timeout begins before a first validation and is not introduced invisibly beneath an already successful cached result
No menu, prompt, database query policy, model, dataset, MAIN pointer or native transcript changes
Observed read-count reuse is a mechanical witness, not an end-to-end speed estimate
